decision: RETAIN current merged baselines for all4 after explicit contextual reassessment; reject all replacement studies
reason_for_reassessment: Earlier boxiness concern over-weighted isolated clay topology for modular stone construction. Actual frozen-painted baseline and placed architectural comparisons show readable distinct roles and coherent ornament; retention is not justified by failed attempts or contract difficulty. Candidate v2 adds810 vs50 triangles with negligible painted reduced gain.

HouseEtc01.rationale: The hooked projecting nose, paired dark eye sockets and flared cheek painting form a clearly recognizable dragon emblem. The rectangular stone block is a deliberate stackable architectural volume; actual stacked30/31 view reads as two repeated heraldic panels with continuous stone courses. Integrated awning surroundings share its restrained warm stone and carved trim. It does not require a free-standing sculpture silhouette to serve this role.
HouseEtc01.limits: Essentially original coarse relief geometry with prior painting treatment; isolated clay looks simplified and strong oblique close-up exposes reliance on painted depth. Retention applies to ordinary placed game-camera use, not a hero close-up sculpture standard.

StoneMuWall02.rationale: The narrow pointed end profile and compact carved crest distinguish the wall terminal from the broad shield modules. The long taper and restrained panel center give the gate assembly a readable ending without competing with portcullis/dragon shields. Existing upper carving and border painting are adequate at assembly scale.
StoneMuWall02.limits: Fine crest anatomy stays mainly painted. Broad-side panel is deliberately quiet; retaining it is not a claim of additional sculptural detail. Two previously documented inherited custom-normal incidents remain baseline, not repaired.

StoneMuWall03.rationale: The broad projecting shield face, sloped cap and lower point have a distinctive defensive outline. Repeated dragon noses/eye shadows read as a consistent fortification motif in the actual south-gate assembly; horizontal ornamental bands and matched warm stone connect the shields to plain wall spans and gate piers. The facade stays legible without added recessed islands.
StoneMuWall03.limits: Close oblique inspection exposes coarse cheek planes and painted small ornament. Repeated motif is intentional modular rhythm rather than unique sculpture; no new geometry improvement is claimed.

StoneMuWall04.rationale: The same shield face deliberately matches03 while the rear wooden firing platform, ladder, chest and iron cannon supply a separate readable function. Siege-wall rear context clearly separates wood from stone and iron; front retains matching sloped cap and pointed crest rhythm. Current combined design is coherent and visually useful.
StoneMuWall04.limits: Front relief has03 close-up limitations; dark cannon remains diffuse iron and was separately reviewed, not assumed an additive error. Rear attachments remain unchanged; no new sculptural detail claimed.

limits: Offline diffuse/placement evidence only; user-reported baseline client result remains distinct from personal observation.
No replacement study is counted as a completed remake.
This asset-specific retention supersedes earlier provisional production flags, not the factual work-performed categories.
